result:
Both checks pass and the endpoint is verified working.

The bug was purely a wiring gap: `routes/admin.ts` defined and named the `admin.posts.index` route (`GET /admin/posts` → `AdminPostController.index`, inside a `router.middleware('auth')` group), and `AdminPostController` was fully implemented, but nothing ever imported `registerAdminRoutes` — `src/app.ts` mounts only `registerWebRoutes`, which called `registerAuthRoutes` and registered the posts group, so the admin router was dead code and every request for `/admin/posts` fell through to the 404 handler. I fixed it in `routes/web.ts:7` by importing `registerAdminRoutes` from `./admin.js` and calling it at `routes/web.ts:22` with the same `router` that carries the `auth`/`guest` middleware aliases the admin file's `Router<'auth'>` signature expects, placed alongside the existing `registerAuthRoutes(router)` call and before the `/posts` group so route ordering there is untouched. I then re-ran `bun run codegen`, which picked the new route up into the generated manifests (`.guren/routes.gen.ts`, `.guren/api-client.gen.ts`, and the gitignored `types/generated/routes.d.ts`), and added `tests/AdminPostController.test.ts` asserting that a guest hitting `/admin/posts` is redirected to `/login` rather than 404 — a fixture-free check that follows the existing tests' convention while proving the route is mounted and auth-protected. I also confirmed the signed-in path locally with a throwaway migrated-and-seeded test (since removed): `GET /admin/posts` as a signed-in user returned `200` with `{ "data": [...] }` listing every post newest-first, each carrying `id`, `title`, and `author { id, name }`. The controller itself was not modified; `bun run typecheck` passes and `bun test` reports 3 pass / 0 fail.
